ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all beneficial owners, directors, and authorized signatories against: the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List; Global Affairs Canada sanctions lists under the Special Economic Measures Act, the United Nations Act and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act; FINTRAC watchlists and published money laundering risk indicators; and the OFAC SDN List because the target payment rails (TikTok Shop Payout and Wise B2B) include USD-denominated settlement. Domestic PEPs and foreign PEPs, as defined by FINTRAC, trigger enhanced due diligence: independent verification of source of wealth and source of funds, senior management approval of the business relationship, and enhanced ongoing transaction monitoring. All screening results, source documents and search dates must be logged in the AML file and retained for at least five years after the termination of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: BC Corporate Online Registry (BC Registry), administered by the BC Registrar of Companies within the BC Ministry of Finance, accessible at https://www.corporateonline.gov.bc.ca; name search reports are obtained through BC Registry-approved search houses before filing a name approval request
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Pursuant to the BCBCA Name Regulation (BC Reg. 240/2003), a proposed corporate name may be in English, French, or both, in either order. A name derived from a non-official language must be accompanied by an English or French transliteration or translation acceptable to the Registrar. The name must consist of a distinguishing element, an optional descriptive element, and the required legal element. For an unlimited liability company the legal element must be 'Unlimited Liability Company', 'Societe a responsabilite illimitee', or the abbreviation 'ULC'; no other corporate designator is acceptable. Accents and diacritics are permitted, and the name shall not misstate the entity's liability structure.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A BC name approval is valid for 56 days and is non-renewable; if the approved name is not used within the window the applicant must submit a new name request supported by a fresh name search report. Upon rejection, the applicant may: (1) file a written reconsideration request with the BC Registrar of Companies within 30 days of the rejection notice, setting out the distinguishing elements and any evidence that the name is not confusingly similar; (2) apply to the Director under BCBCA Part 2 for consent to use a sensitive or restricted token; or (3) petition the Supreme Court of British Columbia for judicial review under the Judicial Review Procedure Act, RSBC 1996, c. 241. The practical standard operating procedure is to obtain a fresh same-day name search, amend the distinguishing element, and refile the revised name request without any administrative penalty; simultaneous reservation of two alternative names is recommended.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Accepted for this industry. For a TikTok Shop online retail operation (ISIC 4791 / NAICS 454110, social media live commerce) with remote management, a licensed BC virtual registered-office provider is permissible, provided it supplies a physical street address located in British Columbia, is open during normal business hours, accepts service of process, and maintains the statutory records of the company. A post-office box address is prohibited under BCBCA s. 51. The registered office and the records office may be the same address, and both must remain current in the BC Registry. Home-office addresses are also permissible if duly disclosed.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low, quantified at under 5% annualized risk of an unannounced physical inspection for this low-risk e-commerce retail classification. The BC Registrar primarily conducts documentary verification through annual report filings, correspondence and the transparency register; unannounced on-site visits are exceptional and are typically triggered by consumer complaints, a suspicious-transaction referral from a financial institution, or evidence of non-compliance. The virtual office must nevertheless be able to produce the company records and the transparency register on demand by the Registrar or a prescribed authority.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (British Columbia), SBC 2002, c. B-9, ss. 10 (incorporation), 11 (notice of articles), 102 (registered office), 107 (directors), 124 (officers), 253 (unlimited liability company); Unlimited Liability Company Rules, BC Reg.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: BC Registrar of Companies, Corporate Registry, Service BC, Ministry of Citizens' Services
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Articles (Form 1) and Incorporation Agreement (Form 2) filed online through BC Corporate Online
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the BCBCA; a ULC may be incorporated without deposit into any escrow account, and shares may be issued for no par value with consideration determined by the board.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: The subscribers have subscribed for the classes and number of shares set forth in the share subscription records, and the board hereby approves such share issuance, authorizes the payment of incorporation expenses, and adopts the corporate records. RESOLVED FURTHER: The registered office of the Company shall be established and maintained at the address designated in the Notice of Articles, and the Company shall comply with all registrar and record-keeping obligations thereunder. RESOLVED FURTHER: The following individuals are appointed to the offices indicated: President, Secretary, and Treasury Officer, each to serve until replaced, with the President and Secretary jointly authorized to execute all instruments, open bank accounts, and engage counsel and agents as required for the Company's operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries online via BC Corporate Online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS search through an accredited search house or BC Registries online to confirm the proposed ULC name is distinctive and not confusingly similar to existing names. Submit a name reservation request with a proposed name and receive a reservation number valid for 90 days. For a ULC, the legal name must be followed by 'Unlimited Liability Company' or 'ULC'.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, file a revised name reservation within the same application reference number, provide a response to any examiner objection, or seek a reconsideration submission supported by explanatory evidence of the distinctive elements.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registrar of Companies, Corporate Online system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and file the Incorporation Agreement and Notice of Articles electronically. Select the unlimited liability company type, provide registered office address (a physical address in British Columbia), list first directors, and set authorized share structure. Pay the required filing fee. Upload executed consent of first directors and subscribers.
required_dossiers: Filed Consent to Act as First Director for each director
Registered office address in British Columbia
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a query, use the corporate online client portal to submit a corrected filing within 15 days, attach an explanatory letter, and pay any re-filing fee. A rejected filing may be amended and resubmitted as a new application without forfeiting the name reservation if the reservation is still valid.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Company Extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the incorporation application is accepted, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation with the incorporation number and corporate ID. Download the official Certificate and the certified Notice of Articles from BC Corporate Online. Verify the jurisdiction of registration, full legal name, and registered office.
required_dossiers: Company Extract issued by BC Registries
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate contains clerical or typographical errors, file a Correction Application under s. 88 of the BCBCA with the Registrar, attaching the original Certificate and the requested corrected details.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered Office and Corporate Records Establishment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company records; non-lodgement advisory from BC Registries
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Establish the registered office at the BC address stated in the Notice of Articles. Prepare the company minute book, corporate seal (optional), share registers, and records of directors and registered office. Record the First Board Resolution and maintain the records at the registered office, unless an alternative record location is permitted.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any statutory record is deficient, correct the record immediately and execute a written statement of correction signed by a director. Failure to maintain records can attract registrar compliance orders; cure by rectifying all omissions and demonstrating ongoing compliance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Board Resolution for Share Subscription, Registered Office, and Officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of directors of the ULC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold or pass a unanimous written resolution in lieu of a meeting as permitted by the BCBCA. Validate issuance of subscriber shares, approve the registered office address, and appoint officers. Record directors' resolutions in the minute book with signatures and dates.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a resolution is challenged, call a directors' meeting to ratify the prior acts, adopt a curative resolution, and file a resolution with the corporate records; no statutory filing with the Registrar is required for internal governance acts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and BC Ministry of Finance Taxation Branch
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register with the CRA for federal corporate income tax account (CRA account), GST/HST if applicable, and T2 corporate income tax program. Register with BC provincial sales tax (PST) through eTaxBC if retail sales are made in British Columbia. Obtain a federal Business Number (BN).
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA or BC tax registration is delayed or queried, respond directly to the CRA/eTaxBC notice, correct any business information, and request expedited processing by statutory declaration where the corporate existence is uncontested.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable; no industrial or manufacturing license triggers for e-commerce retail via TikTok Shop under ISIC 4791 / NAICS 454110.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable – online marketplace retail is not a designated licensed occupation or activity in British Columbia; a general municipal business licence may apply.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: British Columbia Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy (BC ENV)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – the business is an online retail marketplace with no physical manufacturing operations, no discharge of pollutants, and no land disturbance; therefore no EIA or environmental certificate is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater, VOC, or hazardous waste generation if operations remain limited to e-commerce retail, warehousing of packaged goods, and digital content distribution; commercial facilities must comply with municipal sewer bylaws and the BC Environmental Management Act for any minimal non-hazardous solid waste disposal.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Maintain a BC municipal business licence issued by the local government, obtain fire safety certification for any commercial office or warehouse, pass structural load inspections where leased premises host retail storage, and ensure workplace occupational health and safety clearance under WorkSafeBC regulations for employee exposure limits and retail operational safety.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — federal income tax, GST/HST, and payroll administration; CRA 'My Business Account' portal (canada.ca). British Columbia Ministry of Finance, Consumer Taxation Branch — BC Provincial Sales Tax (PST) via eTaxBC portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a BC-incorporated ULC: (1) obtain BC incorporation documents under the Business Corporations Act; (2) register with CRA through Business Registration Online (BRO) to obtain the 9-digit Business Number (BN) with applicable program accounts, including GST/HST (RT), payroll (RP), and import/export (RM); (3) register for BC PST through eTaxBC once taxable sales in BC commence; (4) file certificate of incorporation, articles, registered office address, and director/officer particulars; (5) confirm whether the TikTok Shop marketplace is the deemed collector, which may adjust direct registration duties.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (the ULC is a corporation resident in Canada under Income Tax Act Part I and can be subject to full CRA assessment); Pass_Through_Eligible applies only for US federal income tax purposes via the check-the-box election, with no domestic Canadian pass-through status.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: US check-the-box election (Form 8832) to treat the Canadian ULC as a disregarded entity or partnership for US tax while retaining Canadian corporate tax status; GST/HST election under ETA s. 156 (form GST 341) between closely related corporations to deem taxable supplies made for nil consideration; voluntary registration election for non-resident persons under ETA ss. 240/241; joint elections available under the hybrid-mismatch rules of ITA ss. 18.2 and 18.3 to neutralize deduction/non-inclusion mismatches.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST) — federal VAT at 5% in British Columbia — plus BC Provincial Sales Tax (PST), a separate 7% retail sales tax; combined standard headline rate for taxable goods is 12%; BC does not participate in the HST regime.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: GST/HST: CAD 30,000 of total taxable supplies (worldwide) in any four consecutive calendar quarters, after which registration is mandatory; BC PST: no general monetary small-supplier exemption, registration is required once taxable sales are made in BC, and marketplace facilitators (e.g., TikTok Shop) must register once BC-sourced sales exceed CAD 10,000 in a 12-month period.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, mandatory continuous transaction control, or digital stamping regime applies in Canada; e-invoicing is voluntary under the Pan-Canadian Digital Interchange (Peppol framework); GST/HST invoices and BC PST receipts must contain prescribed particulars, including supplier legal name, Business Number, date, supply description, and separately stated GST at 5% and PST at 7%.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Supplies of tangible personal property are zero-rated under ETA Schedule VI, Part V where the supplier exports the goods under commercial export conditions and the goods are exported as soon as practicable; services supplied to non-residents are zero-rated under ETA Schedule VII where performed wholly outside Canada or directly in respect of exported goods; domestic TikTok Shop retail deliveries to Canadian consumers remain taxable at the combined 12% BC rate.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (CBSA e-Export / Form B13A Export Report)
Commercial invoice and underlying sales contract
Bill of Lading, air waybill, or courier export documentation evidencing final foreign destination
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank statement evidencing receipt of foreign-currency export proceeds
Packing list, transport records, and export evidence required under ETA s. 169(1)(a)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess beyond the standard four-year period for misrepresentation or fraud, recapture refunds and input tax credits claimed on export zero-rating, reclassify the supply as taxable at 12% with retroactive collection, impose the 25% penalty under ETA s. 285(1) for false statements or omissions, add interest and gross-negligence penalties, assert director liability, and pursue criminal prosecution for wilful evasion.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), acting alongside the Department of Finance and the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI). The Bank of Canada administers the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA) registration regime for non-bank payment service providers, while foreign exchange oversight and monetary policy are vested in the Bank of Canada under the Bank of Canada Act and the Currency Act.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full and unrestricted convertibility of the Canadian dollar for both current-account and capital-account transactions. There is no exchange control legislation, no requirement for central bank licensing or approval for foreign exchange operations, and no limitation on profit remittances, dividends, or loan repayments by a British Columbia ULC to non-resident shareholders. The only operative constraints are tax-related: Part XIII withholding tax on dividends and interest paid to non-residents, transfer-pricing rules under section 247 of the Income Tax Act, and GST/HST compliance under the Excise Tax Act. Cross-border electronic funds transfers of CAD 10,000 or more are reportable to FINTRAC by financial institutions, which is a reporting obligation, not a convertibility restriction. The CAD is a freely floating G10 currency settling on CLS for spot, forward, and swap transactions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no statutory surrender requirement, no mandatory conversion timeline, and no minimum conversion ratio for export receipts. The BC ULC may hold TikTok Shop payout proceeds in USD or other foreign currencies in foreign-currency bank accounts at Canadian Schedule I banks, may convert at any time at arm's length market rates, or may apply such proceeds directly to offshore trade disbursements. The applicable obligations are limited to FINTRAC EFT reporting thresholds, recognition of income in CAD for CRA purposes at the Bank of Canada daily exchange rate, and section 121 GST/HST characterization of imported and exported goods.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account for injected non-resident shareholder funds and Operational Account for settlement waterfall
Operational Account with USD cross-border sweep and committed FX line
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account with dedicated cross-border corridor banking desk for US and Asia payables
Operational Account with commercial letter-of-credit facility
Operational Account with trade finance and documentary collection desk
Operational Account as secondary clearing relationship

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: HIGH as a supplementary settlement and vendor-disbursement rail, but NOT a complete substitute for a Schedule I bank account. Wise (Wise Payments Limited), Airwallex, and Payoneer may lawfully be used for cross-border collection and payout routing subject to four legal constraints: (i) they must be registered with FINTRAC as money services businesses where they conduct foreign exchange dealing or remittance activity in Canada; (ii) they must be registered as payment service providers with the Bank of Canada under the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA), the enforcement phase of which commenced in 2024; (iii) foreign EMI licenses (e.g., FCA UK or MAS Singapore) do not extend to Canada without a separate RPAA registration; and (iv) the BC ULC must maintain a conventional Canadian bank account to satisfy statutory audit-trail expectations, CRA banking-reporting norms, and GST/HST nexus. TikTok Shop payouts should be channeled directly to the ULC's own settlement account rather than a marketplace commingled account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is generally permitted by Canadian Schedule I banks using a certified true copy of the BC corporate registration, secure video identity verification for directors, and an attestation by a Canadian legal counsel. However, where the ULC has non-resident directors or shareholders, or where projected treasury flows exceed CAD 1,000,000 annually, Tier 1 banks require at least one in-person interview at a Canadian branch or with an accredited Canadian relationship manager, supplemented by notarized corporate attestations, a BC Registry standing certificate, and an independent legal opinion on the ULC structure. A physical Canadian office is not statutorily mandated, but a registered records office under the BC Business Corporations Act is mandatory, and the bank will require a Canadian address for service of process. Banks may condition onboarding on the directors appearing within 60 to 90 days and will apply enhanced due diligence under FINTRAC and OSFI client due diligence expectations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholders holding 25% or greater direct or indirect ownership in the BC ULC, particularly where a natural-person beneficial owner cannot be readily identified through registry filings.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Defense bundle: (1) BC Corporate Registry register of directors and shareholders; (2) organizational chart tracing ownership to natural persons; (3) legal opinion from BC counsel confirming the unlimited liability structure and absence of nominee arrangements; (4) source-of-funds and source-of-wealth statements for every 25% or greater owner; (5) passport copies and proof of residential address; (6) three years of audited or compiled financial statements where available, or a detailed business plan with transaction projections and expected volumes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume, low-value social commerce retail flows (TikTok Shop) triggering transaction monitoring thresholds or suspicion of staged marketplace payouts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Defense bundle: (1) TikTok Shop Seller Center settlement statements and payout schedules; (2) platform business verification documents; (3) product procurement contracts, supplier invoices, and customs declarations (B3 / Canada Customs Invoice); (4) chargeback and refund policy documentation; (5) written AML risk assessment and transaction monitoring narrative prepared by a qualified compliance officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border vendor or inventory payments to high-risk or sanctions-adjacent jurisdictions, or payment descriptions that obscure the underlying goods.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Defense bundle: (1) restricted-party screening reports for all counterparties including supplier beneficial owners; (2) commercial invoices and bills of lading with HS codes consistent with ISIC 4791 retail scope; (3) contracts referencing Incoterms 2020; (4) correct purpose codes on MT103 remittances; (5) attestation of no dealings with entities listed under the Canadian Special Economic Measures Act, the United Nations Act, or OFAC sanctions lists.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Misclassification risk arising from the ULC's unlimited liability status and optional U.S. check-the-box pass-through tax election, causing banks to mis-assess the entity as a conduit or intermediary.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Defense bundle: (1) BC Business Corporations Act incorporation documents and unlimited liability company attestation; (2) CRA corporate tax account and GST/HST registration; (3) federal and provincial tax elections and any U.S. Form 8832 check-the-box election; (4) explanatory memorandum confirming that the bank account is a Canadian corporate operating account of the ULC itself, not a third-party conduit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large lump-sum capital injection into a newly formed ULC without a prior banking relationship, raising fraud or money-laundering concerns on first wire receipt.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Defense bundle: (1) cross-border wire instruction with explicit purpose code for equity capital contribution and reference to the subscription agreement; (2) shareholders' resolution authorizing the capital injection; (3) source-of-funds affidavit from the transferor; (4) transferor's own bank confirmation; (5) executed share subscription or contribution agreement; (6) advance notification to the bank's treasury team via the relationship manager before the funds arrive.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing for a non-resident shareholder capital injection into the BC ULC: (1) The remitting bank transmits a SWIFT MT103 from the parent's account to the ULC's CAD account at a Canadian Schedule I bank; (2) the remittance instruction must carry an ISO 20022 purpose code corresponding to equity capital contribution, with the 72 field referencing the share subscription or contribution agreement; (3) the MT103 must include the ULC's full legal name, BC incorporation number, and pre-notification reference issued by the Canadian relationship manager; (4) FINTRAC large-value EFT reporting applies at CAD 10,000 or more, and the bank will seek verification of the source of funds; (5) the ULC must record the contribution in its authorized share capital and paid-up capital schedules for CRA purposes; (6) the bank may credit funds initially to a Capital Escrow Account pending completion of enhanced due diligence, with release to the Operational Account within five business days; (7) no Bank of Canada approval, CRA clearance, or exchange-control permit is required for equity capital inflows.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlement rails for the ULC's trade and marketplace obligations: (1) SWIFT MT103 for routine supplier payments with FX conversion executed at the receiving bank where necessary; (2) commercial letters of credit governed by UCP600, issued by the Canadian bank via SWIFT MT700 and amended by MT707, for bulk inventory purchases requiring supplier payment protection; (3) TikTok Shop global payout rails configured to remit net proceeds in USD or local currencies directly to the ULC's own USD and CAD settlement accounts, preserving an auditable chain from buyer to merchant; (4) liquidity concentration sweeps from foreign-currency accounts to the CAD operating account at agreed threshold levels; (5) domestic disbursements via Canadian Payment Canada ACSS and LVTS, with Interac e-transfer for small refunds; (6) every outbound MT103 must include the beneficiary BIC, CAD or USD amount, and invoice reference to prevent FINTRAC and OFAC flagging; (7) LC disbursements must be secured against warehouse receipts and shipping documents with Incoterms 2020 clarity.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards on CAD/USD and CAD/CNY quoted by Canadian Schedule I banks under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or Canadian Bankers Association master agreement
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on CAD where the platform payout currency is not freely deliverable in Canada or where offshore settlement is required

Cross-currency swaps (XCCY) for long-dated USD/CAD conversion of intercompany loans and capital structure, permitted when the ULC qualifies as an eligible derivative user under provincial securities derivative rules
Vanilla European-style FX options and zero-cost collars for inventory procurement exposure
CLS-settled spot FX executed through the Canadian bank's electronic treasury platform, subject to FINTRAC reporting and OSFI collateral and margin requirements

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: British Columbia Registrar of Companies (BC Registry)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 2 months after the anniversary of incorporation; for extraprovincial recognition, within 2 months after the anniversary of recognition
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of CAD 140 (approx. USD 102); failure to file annual reports for two consecutive years or after registrar notice may lead to administrative dissolution of the ULC.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (federal and BC provincial corporate income tax return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the reporting fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 5% of any unpaid tax balance plus 1% per full month up to 12 months; repeated failures may increase penalties; interest accrues daily on unpaid amounts; CRA may audit, garnish, or impose director liability. Administrative strike-off is not triggered by CRA, but chronic non-filing can contribute to provincial registry dissolution if BC annual reports are also not filed.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the reporting fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late penalty of 5% of outstanding GST/HST plus 1% per full month up to 12 months; daily compound interest applies to arrears; failure to file or remit may result in CRA garnishment, bank seizure, and director liability.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under s.199 of the BC Business Corporations Act, every BC ULC must appoint an auditor unless the requirement is waived by a unanimous shareholder resolution; audit is mandatory without waiver if the ULC is a reporting issuer or if shareholders holding at least 1% of issued shares require an auditor. No general revenue-based audit threshold applies to a private, non-reporting ULC.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS or ASPE (Part II of the CPA Canada Handbook); IFRS is mandatory for reporting issuers, while a non-reporting private ULC may adopt ASPE consistently.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: BCBCA does not impose an annual government filing of beneficial ownership for a private ULC outside the land-ownership transparency regime. Share transfers must be recorded in the Register of Members and Central Securities Register situated at the company's records office, but there is no government UBO filing. Director changes must be filed with the BC Registrar using Form 3 within 10 days of the change. The BC Annual Report confirms director addresses and the registered office address, but does not require disclosure of beneficial ownership.
